final.memo:
Yahoo! is a classic case where underlying asset value is being obscured by a board and leadership team that lack the basic credibility required to oversee a public company. Our analysis of SEC filings has uncovered unacceptable discrepancies regarding the academic credentials of the CEO and director Patti Hart, a failure of disclosure that strikes at the heart of the board's integrity [D03, D07]. We did not invest for the management to be caught in a biography scandal; we invested for the intelligent monetization of Asian assets and the recovery of core operating value [D01, D08].

The current board has failed the most basic test of governance. While the company points to stabilized revenue as a sign of progress, these figures cannot mask the deeper rot in management oversight [D02, D04]. A company with high-value products cannot flourish under a leadership team that lacks a transparent, truthful control process [D01, D06]. We are not interested in waiting for the current regime to stumble through further disclosures; we are escalating to ensure our four independent director candidates are seated to provide the technical and media expertise this business desperately needs [D03, D07, D08].

Our case is clear: replace the entrenched actors who have presided over this degradation with directors who understand shareholder stewardship [D07]. The path to 20-30% IRR remains, but it is now contingent on a board refresh [D07, D08]. We are moving to the next stage of our campaign because the mispricing persists, the shareholder base is receptive to change, and the annual meeting represents the immediate window for intervention [D07]. We exit the era of quiet dialogue and demand a board that adheres to the standards our capital expects [D07, D08].
